requestedBy: human user in LAX / Hollywood — multihost architecture
status: required; design and implementation pending; existing retained-input checkpoint primitives are partial foundations
intent: Offer manual, reviewed context rotation: mark useful material during work, review and edit an explicit seed, then discard the active window and start a genuinely fresh window while preserving durable agent identity.
userRequirement: I'd like lax to offer manual context management with a "Mark as you go" and "review before refresh" approach, which allows us to discard a window entirely, start fresh, while maintaining agent identity to an extent. This allows us to ensure that all the context the user believes is important is preserved, and allows structured data like goals and plans and roles to all be explicitly carried over or even edited between window changes. Context generated by the model and the user in the last window may not have been present at the beginning and can be valuable to add to the next fresh context. Keep track of the seed size. Preserving the entire window should remain possible for someone who needs it.

requirements: Keep agent identity, authorized room memberships, role bindings, host/workspace identity and work/delivery ownership separate from the disposable model window.
Record window identity, generation and seed revision. A fresh window is not a replacement agent or duplicate task. Preserve old window history for audit and authorized retrieval.
For a three-context agent, track reader/writer/responder windows and seeds independently under the same agent. Shared canonical responsibilities remain versioned references.
Allow the user to pin relevant user inputs, public agent outputs, discoveries, decisions, tool/action evidence and artifact references from the current window.
Permit model-proposed additions as visible, attributable proposals; new valuable knowledge learned during this window can enter the next seed even when absent from the original seed.
Persist exact source identity/version or digest, author, selection reason, intended purpose and ordering. User-pinned material cannot silently disappear through summarization or size trimming.
Provide a durable editable seed draft and preview of the exact proposed next model-visible input, including additions/removals and changed canonical revisions.

Allow review-time edits to roles, goals, plans and other structured context through their authorized versioned canonical APIs. Human-authored notes and edits retain authorship; do not rewrite historical messages or create a second authoritative copy of a goal/plan/role.

Reconcile canonical edits and seed freeze with explicit receipts. A partially applied canonical edit and an uninstalled or unknown window remain distinguishable; do not promise a single atomic transaction across database and native process.

Freeze an approved seed by source IDs, versions/hashes and native configuration. Commit only at a safe native boundary. Incoming messages and unfinished work remain durable throughout preview, review and installation.
Construct the next window deterministically from current mandatory native instructions/tool policy, selected canonical structured state and approved retained material.
Do not force preservation of the entire closing transcript or require a lossy automatic narrative summary. Preserve selected new facts and their original source evidence.

Offer an explicit carry-entire-available-window option when authorized and feasible. Validate real capacity and headroom; reject impossible seeds before closing the current window, rather than silently dropping material.
Ensure the actual provider request/window is fresh; retaining logical agent/thread identity must not accidentally retain omitted context through stale incremental provider state.
Show and persist seed size per window/purpose: selected content bytes, total assembled input/overhead bytes, estimated tokens with estimator/model identity, and capacity/headroom.

Record authoritative initial-input token usage when available from the next actual admitted request, with its scope distinguished from estimated seed-only counts. Do not start a model or audio connection merely to measure the seed.
Track initial seed size and subsequent window growth so repeated refreshes do not quietly accumulate an ever-growing seed.
Reauthorize selected sources and canonical revisions at commit. A changed permission, source, user stop or cancellation must be explicit; a mark is not an access grant.

Preserve pending input, drafts, unanswered questions, accepted work, active/unfinished tool operations and unknown delivery receipts. Context rotation never authorizes replaying a command or external action.
Recover the same original installation operation and exact receipts after disconnect or restart. Unknown outcomes stay held until resolved; no exactly-once claim.
Manual-review mode must have explicit behavior near hard context limits (for example pausing for review). It must not silently substitute an automatic lossy compaction that discards user marks.
Offer this mode without switching all live agents or defaults during its design/qualification.

responsibilities.LAX: Selection/review/seed model, purpose-aware window lifecycle, native preflight and installation, provider-request reset, identity preservation and model-visible/tool contract.
responsibilities.Hollywood: Durable attributable marks/seed manifests and review/control records using existing canonical context/work/role and operation mechanisms, with source permissions and receipt recovery.
responsibilities.NextComp: Mark controls on eligible messages/activity, seed preview/diff/edit/review and refresh controls, per-purpose seed size/freshness and honest installation state.
responsibilities.CodexUpstream: Reference implementation only. Fresh main inspected at970111f6cb62cc02fe36a82ea7d71b37a2889c97; compaction trigger belongs to harness, so LAX can replace that policy without requiring provider-managed automatic compaction.

implementationSequence: Reconcile existing retained selection/native checkpoint APIs against this requirement; explicitly identify the missing human mark/review/size and multi-purpose surfaces.
Implement durable seed draft/preview/freeze/commit contracts with exact source provenance and canonical role/goal/plan revisions; reuse existing operations and native owner receipts.

Prove a headless authorized-human API journey with actual model work: learn a new fact during windowA, mark it plus a user correction, review/edit structured state, refresh to windowB, and finish the same work using the new fact.
Expose the qualified controls and seed-size information in NextComp, including offline drafts/reconnect and pending-install recovery.

Qualify whole-window choice, oversized refusal before closure, cancellation/permission/revision races and same-operation restart recovery; then enable this mode explicitly for a selected agent before considering defaults.
acceptance: User-selected material and newly learned closing-window facts appear in the reviewed seed and the actual next provider input with exact source provenance.
Unselected closing-window material is absent from the fresh request while original history remains retrievable under its permissions.
An edited goal, plan or role is the intended adopted canonical revision in the next window; work ownership/identity and original operations remain intact.
An actual model continues the same deliverable after refresh and correctly uses the marked new fact. Mechanical inclusion and semantic success are reported separately.
Preview/seed size and final native installation agree; oversize or changed-source/permission rejection leaves the current window usable and pending work intact.
Restart/disconnect observations reconcile the original checkpoint without another command execution or new work submission.
Three-context qualification preserves distinct purpose histories, relevant shared state and queued messages without a reader/writer/responder dependency cycle.
NextComp users can mark, review, edit and refresh through the supported human interface; automated tests exercise that interface and distinguish native UI, provider and physical-phone evidence.
